question.:question/problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $w,$ given by

$$
(r-3)w-6=-5
$$

where $r$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $r?$

$r=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, let's write our equation in the form $aw=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-3)w-6 & =-5 \\ (r-3)w-6+6 & =-5+6 \\ {{(r-3)}_{⏟}}_{a}w & ={{1}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
r-3=0.
$$

Solving this for $r,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r-3 & =0 \\ r & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
ax=b
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(q+5)v+6 & =-4 \\ 2(q+5)v+6-6 & =-4-6 \\ {{2(q+5)}_{⏟}}_{a}v & ={{-10}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}

$$
